text:
A: Alright. Gary. Dagenham.
B: Tomasz. Peterborough.
A: Peterborough. Been through it. On the A1.
B: Everybody goes through it. Nobody stops.
A: Ha. Fair enough. What d'you do, then?
B: Electrician. Team leader for engineering in food factory. Chilled food, sandwiches, ready meals.
A: Proper trade, that. I'm in an office at a skip firm in Rainham. Phones, invoices. Used to be in the yard till my back went.
B: Skip firm. You have a lot of vans, then.
A: Lorries, vans. Van got another ULEZ fine last week. Twelve fifty a day, they want, just to drive round your own manor. It's daylight robbery. Boss went mental.
B: We don't have this in Peterborough. Only the petrol. Tesco garage, every week more.
A: Every week more. Don't get me started on the council.
B: No, I also have opinions. Neighbour parks across my drive. Again. I go out at five for early shift, I cannot get the car out.
A: Same! Bloke on my street nicks my space every night. I've lived there twenty-odd years. He's been there six months.
B: You should leave note.
A: I've left notes. He don't read. What d'you drive?
B: BMW. Five Series, old one, second-hand. I do it up myself. Just got the alloys off Facebook Marketplace, eighteen inch, very good condition. He wanted three hundred, I paid one eighty.
A: One eighty? Good effort. I'm on Marketplace all the time, me. Tools mostly. Bloke tried to mug me off on a drill last week, forty quid for a knackered one. I said fifteen or I walk. He took fifteen.
B: Is the only way. If you look like you want it, you pay too much.
A: That's it exactly. You do much on the side? Cash jobs, like?
B: Why you ask this?
A: Just asking, mate. Not the taxman.
B: Okay. Weekends, sometimes. Consumer unit, rewire, small things. Honestly, people doing only house jobs earn more than me. I think about it. Self-employed.
A: Do it. I would if I had a trade. I've got nothing. Never had a proper job for life like my old man. Ford, Dagenham, thirty years.
B: Ford. Is still there?
A: Engines, bits. Not like it was. Whole area's changed.
B: Everywhere is changed. I came in 2005. Wisbech, packhouse, agency. Now I am team leader. So.
A: Twenty years? You're basically from here then.
B: No. I am Polish who lives here. My kids, yes, they are English. They talk like you.
A: Ha, God help 'em. You into football?
B: Premier League. Polish national team. You are West Ham, I think? I saw in the photo, the cushion.
A: West Ham, yeah. Gave the season ticket up when they moved to that soulless bowl. Watch it on the laptop now, on a dodgy stream.
B: Soulless bowl. I will use this. My son says same about—
